title: What If Every Car in America Went Electric?

scenes.text: What if every car in America went electric? Everyone fears the power grid. The numbers are less scary.
Americans drive about 2.9 trillion miles a year in cars and light trucks. The average electric car covers 3.1 miles per kilowatt-hour.
Powering all of that takes roughly 950 billion kilowatt-hours a year, about 22 percent more electricity than the US generates.
Germany lands close: Fraunhofer calculates that all 45 million German cars switching would add about 20 percent.
Fleets turn over slowly, so generation would need to grow only about one percent a year. Over 70 years it has averaged 3.2.
The real strain is local. One home charger draws 11 to 22 kilowatts, so smart charging at night is the fix.
